messages:
Maria (Sales): Heads-up — ShadowBank is ready to kick a week-long POC. They want our Private deployment inside their VPC and they enforce perimeter TLS inspection (DPI). Asks: 1) Can PrivateLink work with TLS inspect + preserve their audit logs? 2) Static egress IPs (for allowlist) — what do we provide? 3) Short firewall snippet they can paste into their questionnaire. Timeline: start next Tue. @Sam (Solutions) @Raj (NetOps)

Sam (Solutions): Quick take: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is usually the better security posture — no public-facing ELBs. But TLS inspection breaks end-to-end TLS unless the customer terminates TLS before inspection or we terminate inside their VPC. Two practical approaches:
1) PrivateLink + customer-side TLS passthrough to their DPI (they keep control of certs). Our interface endpoints are IPs in their VPC subnets. We will need outbound egress to our control plane and model endpoints.
2) VPC peering (or transit) with a small connector deployed in customer VPC that handles egress back to Redwood — preserves client-srcip if they need it.

Sam (Solutions): For the static egress IP ask: we offer a static egress IP add-on (managed NAT) for Private deployments. It’s an extra monthly line item; policy: one static /32 per customer-region or a small pool for HA. If they need many IPs we recommend Dedicated (reserved capacity) with NAT gateway mapping — pricing increases.

Raj (NetOps): Important network details + firewall snippet they can paste: 

```
# ShadowBank -> Redwood POC allowlist (example)
#  - Allow outbound from customer subnets hosting our interface endpoints / connectors
#  - Replace <REDFW_EGRESS_IPS> with the static egress IPs we provide

# Allow interface endpoint traffic (PrivateLink)
ALLOW tcp from 10.0.32.0/24 to 10.2.5.0/24 port 443

# Allow outbound to Redwood control plane & model egress
ALLOW tcp from <customer_subnets> to <REDFW_EGRESS_IPS> ports 443, 9411

# DNS / NTP if required
ALLOW udp from <customer_subnets> to 8.8.8.8 port 53
ALLOW udp from <customer_subnets> to <ntp_pool> port 123
```

Raj (NetOps): Notes: PrivateLink endpoints are interface ENIs in the customer subnets — those are the addresses they see locally. Our service side will still egress to the internet (or our backbone) and that traffic will originate from Redwood-managed egress IPs. If they require TLS inspection to see the payload, the customer must either terminate TLS before the inspection or we provide a connector in their VPC to hand traffic to their DPI.

Emily (SE): From the security questionnaire perspective: add these bullets to Qs: 
- Data in transit: TLS 1.2+ for our control plane; mTLS available for connectors.
- We don't persist customer request content by default unless they opt into logs; you can ask for a data retention SLA in the contract.
- For TLS-inspect workflows, recommend a dedicated connector deployment so they retain visibility and logs.

Sam (Solutions): Pricing shorthand to share with customer: static egress IP add-on = $X/month per IP (ops quote pending), connector deployment is billed as a small VM + networking (one-off + runtime). Dedicated reserved capacity changes token/throughput pricing — I’ll pull exact numbers.

Maria (Sales): Can you drop the rough number in the thread? Customer wants it for security committee packet.

Sam (Solutions): Rough numbers: static egress IP add-on: $2,500/month per IP (example quote), connector VM: ~$600/month + one-time setup $1,500. Dedicated reserved capacity: starts ~ $25k/month for baseline (sizing dependent). I’ll notate these as estimates until quoting.

deploy-bot: New ticket created: INT-1142 (POC: ShadowBank — egress IPs, firewall snippet, pricing estimates).

Raj (NetOps): One more gotcha — SNI-based routing. If the customer's DPI rewrites SNI or terminates TLS, we need to validate JWT/certificate flows with their app owners. Also confirm whether they will intercept cert chains — this can break mutual auth.

Emily (SE): For the questionnaire, add a one-paragraph example that the customer can paste: 

"Redwood will deploy an interface endpoint (PrivateLink) into customer-managed subnets. Outbound model requests from the endpoint will egress from Redwood-managed static IPs (provided as part of the POC). If the customer performs TLS inspection, they must ensure certificate chains are reconstructed for mutual-TLS endpoints or deploy a connector in their VPC so inspection occurs pre-ingress."

Maria (Sales): Great — I’ll put the snippet and estimate in the packet. Action items: Sam to confirm exact egress IP list and formal quote (by EOD Fri), Raj to produce a one-page network diagram (by Mon), Emily to draft the security blurb for the questionnaire. I’ll sync with ShadowBank and schedule the kickoff. :thumbsup:

Sam (Solutions): Acknowledged — on it.

Raj (NetOps): Acknowledged — will drop a diagram and the minimal subnet/cidr requirements.

Maria (Sales): Thanks everyone — tagging later if we need legal/Security review.
